1.s: “Blessed be… God of all comfort; who comforts us in all our affliction, that we may be able to comfort those who are in any affliction.” Paul explains his change of plans.
1.d: “However many are the promises of God, in him is the ‘Yes’” [[bible:2 Corinthians 1:20]]. God is faithful, so his promises in Christ can be trusted [[tosn:2 Corinthians 1:18-20]], and the Holy Spirit makes his people sure of them [[bsn:2 Corinthians 1:12-22]].

2.s: Paul wrote a painful letter out of love; now the offender should be forgiven and comforted. We are the aroma of Christ.
2.d: After a painful visit, Paul wrote a letter “with many tears”; that letter seems to have been lost [[tosn:2 Corinthians 2:3-4]]. The church then disciplined the man who had wronged Paul, and Paul now asks them to forgive and welcome him back [[tosn:2 Corinthians 2:5-11]] [[bsn:2 Corinthians 1:23-2:11]].

3.s: The Corinthians are a letter from Christ written by the Spirit. The new covenant is more glorious than Moses’s; “where the Spirit of the Lord is, there is liberty.”
3.d: Moses’ face shone after he spoke with the Lord (Exodus 34:29–35) [[tosn:2 Corinthians 3:7-11]]. Paul contrasts the old covenant written on stone with the new covenant written on human hearts (Jeremiah 31:33) [[tosn:2 Corinthians 3:4-18]].

4.s: “We have this treasure in clay vessels.” “Pressed on every side, yet not crushed.” “The things which are seen are temporal, but the things which are not seen are eternal.”
4.d: “We have this treasure in clay vessels” [[bible:2 Corinthians 4:7]]: this gives purpose to suffering [[tosn:2 Corinthians 4:7]]. Paul and his companions faced constant danger, and the resurrection gave them hope to keep going [[bsn:2 Corinthians 4:1-18]].

5.s: Our earthly tent will be replaced by a heavenly dwelling. “If anyone is in Christ, he is a new creation.” God gave us the ministry of reconciliation: “Be reconciled to God.”
5.d: “Him who knew no sin he made to be sin on our behalf; so that in him we might become the righteousness of God” [[bible:2 Corinthians 5:21]]. Christ never sinned (John 8:46; 1 Peter 2:22) [[tosn:2 Corinthians 5:21]], and his ambassadors call people to be made right with God through him [[tosn:2 Corinthians 5:18-21]].

6.s: “Now is the acceptable time… now is the day of salvation.” Paul lists his hardships. “Don’t be unequally yoked with unbelievers.”
6.d: “Now is the day of salvation” [[bible:2 Corinthians 6:2]]: the quotation is from Isaiah 49:8 [[tosn:2 Corinthians 6:2]]. In 6:18 Paul quotes 2 Samuel 7:14 and adds daughters as well as sons (compare Isaiah 43:6) [[tosn:2 Corinthians 6:18]].

7.s: Paul rejoices at Titus’s news that the Corinthians repented. “godly sorrow produces repentance to salvation.”
7.d: “Godly sorrow produces repentance to salvation… But the sorrow of the world produces death” [[bible:2 Corinthians 7:10]]. Sorrow without repentance leads to spiritual death; sorrow that turns from sin leads to salvation [[tosn:2 Corinthians 7:9-10]], and the Corinthians’ sorrow changed how they lived [[bsn:2 Corinthians 7:2-16]].

8.s: The Macedonians gave generously out of poverty. “Though he was rich, yet for your sakes he became poor.”
8.d: “Though he was rich, yet for your sakes he became poor” [[bible:2 Corinthians 8:9]]: the Lord himself is the model for generous giving [[tosn:2 Corinthians 8:9]]. Paul hoped this gift from Gentile churches to the Jewish believers would bind the two together [[tosn:2 Corinthians 8:1-9:15]].

9.s: “God loves a cheerful giver.” Generosity leads to thanksgiving to God.
9.d: Believers give because everything they have is a gift from God, and the believers in Jerusalem would praise God for the gift [[bsn:2 Corinthians 9:6-15]]. Paul sent helpers ahead so that the Corinthians’ promised gift would be ready [[tosn:2 Corinthians 9:1-5]].

10.s: Paul defends his ministry: his weapons are spiritual, “bringing every thought into captivity to the obedience of Christ,”
10.d: His critics said his letters were “weighty and strong, but his bodily presence is weak” [[bible:2 Corinthians 10:10]]. Some missionaries opposed to Paul had come to Corinth [[tosn:2 Corinthians 10:1-13:13]], and they mistook his gentleness for weakness [[tosn:2 Corinthians 10:1]].

11.s: Paul, speaking “as a fool”, lists his sufferings: beatings, shipwrecks, dangers, sleepless nights and his anxiety for the churches.
11.d: Paul was imprisoned many times (for example Acts 16:22–23); some of these hardships are recorded in Acts [[tosn:2 Corinthians 11:23-24]] [[tosn:2 Corinthians 11:23-27]]. He earned his living by making tents rather than relying on new churches [[tosn:2 Corinthians 11:7]].

12.s: Paul was caught up to the third heaven, but was given “a thorn in the flesh”. God said, “My grace is sufficient for you, for my power is made perfect in weakness.”
12.d: We do not know what Paul’s thorn in the flesh was; we know only that it kept him humble [[tosn:2 Corinthians 12:7-10]]. The Lord answered, “My grace is sufficient for you, for my power is made perfect in weakness” [[bible:2 Corinthians 12:9]].

13.s: Paul warns he will not spare them, urges them to examine themselves, and ends with a blessing: “The grace of the Lord Jesus Christ, God’s love, and the fellowship of the Holy Spirit be with you all.”
13.d: “The grace of the Lord Jesus Christ, God’s love, and the fellowship of the Holy Spirit be with you all” [[bible:2 Corinthians 13:14]]. Christ’s love reconciles us to the Father, and the Spirit unites us with all believers [[tosn:2 Corinthians 13:14]] [[bsn:2 Corinthians 12:21-13:14]].
